root_causes.root_cause: LLM audit judge applies image-enrichment-completeness criterion to hierarchical (non-flat) documents, but classify_verdict at helpers.py:1244 only tracks image_enrichment_ratio for flat docs (content_class flat_prose/flat_mixed via the image_enrichment_promoted gate at line 1274). For hierarchical docs (content_class='' or 'unknown'), classify_verdict is called at client.py:1518 with image_enrichment_ratio=None and content_class='', so unenriched <!-- image --> markers in tree node text are invisible to the code-level gate. The stored verdict correctly returns PASS (502 nodes, depth 4, good max_leaf_ratio), but the LLM audit judge sees 12 unenriched image markers and downgrades to MARGINAL. This is a gate-vs-judge alignment gap, not a code bug in classify_verdict itself.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Either (a) extend classify_verdict to accept an image_marker_count / unenriched_marker_count for hierarchical docs and apply a soft penalty (e.g., downgrade to MARGINAL if unenriched_ratio > threshold), OR (b) align the LLM audit judge prompt to not penalize decorative/seal image markers in hierarchical docs where text extraction is complete. Option (b) is simpler and arguably more correct since the 12 markers are likely decorative seals/logos in a 502-node/110k-char document with zero content loss.
